findings.description: Critical: The ADDED scenario requires “the bounded apply result” to report escalation resolutions, and contracts/README.md says “the observable Python return value adds a bounded escalation_resolutions list while preserving existing keys.” Design D1/D4 and tasks 2.1–2.3 intentionally keep ExecutionAdapter.apply’s return shape unchanged and put resolutions on a separate route_parked_escalations method. That contradiction invites folding routing into apply (or mutating apply’s return), which collapses the apply/route retry boundary and can replay dispatch_fn after an already-acknowledged apply.
findings.resolution: Rewrite the scenario and contracts note so escalation_resolutions (or equivalent) is solely the return of route_parked_escalations; add an explicit SHALL that apply MUST NOT invoke gate routing and MUST retain its current keys (batch_id, completed/failed/parked_item_ids, gate_decisions).

findings.description: Critical: Design D5’s central invariant—if gate routing fails after durable parking, the host retries only route_parked_escalations and never re-invokes apply/dispatch_fn—has no ADDED WHEN/THEN scenario. Spec coverage stops at happy-path routing, notify, auto resume, prior-record, and exclusions, so the failure/retry contract that justifies splitting the operations is not executable or enforceable.
findings.resolution: Add a scenario: AFTER apply has parked a policy_pause and released its lease, WHEN route_parked_escalations raises, THEN the attempt remains parked with effects_applied intact, a subsequent apply of the same batch is refused or is not attempted by the host protocol, and recovery is only by re-calling route_parked_escalations (prior-record prevents duplicate notify/audit).

findings.description: Critical: Tasks 1.1–1.4 and the design Test Strategy prove post-persist ordering, auto/notify paths, prior-record reuse, and exclusions, but never require a RED assertion that dispatch_fn call count stays at 1 when routing fails after a successful apply. Without that guard, an implementer can “fix” routing by retrying apply and still satisfy the listed tests.
findings.resolution: Add an explicit failing test (and Test Strategy item) that applies a policy_pause once, forces route_parked_escalations to raise, asserts dispatch_fn was called exactly once, and shows a second route_parked_escalations recovers without a second apply.

findings.description: Nit: Partial-batch behavior for route_parked_escalations is unspecified. If a batch has multiple policy_pause attempts and resolve_parked succeeds (including resume) for the first then raises on the second, retry correctly skips the no-longer-parked first attempt, but the plan never states whether the method is best-effort per attempt, must fail before any resume, or must return partial escalation_resolutions collected before the error. Implementers will guess, and hosts cannot report degradations deterministically.
findings.resolution: Specify fail-closed-per-attempt semantics: process matched attempts in stable order, persist each resolve_parked side effect immediately, on error re-raise after recording which dispatch_ids already resolved, and document that retries resume from still-parked policy_pause rows only.

findings.description: Nit: Idempotent handling of an already-proceeded decision is incomplete for the new method. Existing gate_router tests show a reused proceed still calls adapter.resume while the attempt remains parked; after a successful resume the attempt is prepared, so a retried route_parked_escalations scan omits it and returns no resolution for that dispatch_id. The ADDED “Repeated reconciliation” scenario only covers blocked prior-record reuse, not the already-resumed case the host must observe after a crash between resume and returning the bounded list.
findings.resolution: Add a scenario/test: after auto proceed+resume, a second route_parked_escalations for the same batch neither re-notifies nor resumes again, and either reports the prior proceed from the gate ledger or documents that absence from the parked scan means already-routed.

findings.description: Nit: Notify-with-timeout acceptance requires the “supervisor mirror and rehydrated handoff” to carry the escalate_resume pending gate, and task 3.1 tells authors to retain gates in “the cycle’s supervisor handoff.” Execute today does not write a coordinator supervisor handoff; gate_router._project writes only the tracked mirror, and rehydrate prefers the newer of handoff vs mirror. The plan never states whether execute must emit a handoff after routing or whether mirror projection alone satisfies rehydration—leaving a false requirement to add handoff writes or an untested durability gap.
findings.resolution: Clarify that resolve_parked’s mirror projection is the execute-time durability path, that the next rehydrate MUST surface the pending gate/deadline from that mirror when no newer handoff exists, and only require an execute handoff write if that is an intentional new obligation.

findings.description: Optional: Design does not require route_parked_escalations to run under ExecutionAdapter’s @_serialized_transition advisory lock, unlike apply/resume/reconcile. Concurrent reconcile/resume against the same workspace during a multi-attempt route scan could observe torn checkpoint state even though individual resume calls are locked.
findings.resolution: Prefer decorating route_parked_escalations with @_serialized_transition (or document why per-attempt resume locking is sufficient and the scan is read-only until resolve_parked).

findings.description: FYI: Because route_parked_escalations delegates to gate_router.resolve_parked → ApprovalGate.evaluate, a notify_with_timeout posture synchronously files, notifies, and polls until timeout T inside the execute host—potentially once per exhausted dispatch in the batch. This matches existing gate-check/resolve_parked behavior and is acceptable if intentional, but the plan never calls out the blocking cost on the supervise execute path.
findings.resolution: Document in design/SKILL.md that immediate escalation routing inherits the synchronous notify poll window, and that multiple policy_pause attempts serialize those waits.

findings.description: Post-persist separation is sound: apply remains the exact-result/apply_delegated_batch transaction that parks policy_pause and releases the lease; routing is a mandatory host-invoked follow-on through the existing gate_router.resolve_parked seam with prior-record reuse, authorized resume CAS, and exclusion of ordinary pending_gate, failed, and quarantined attempts.

Feasibility checks against the current code hold: apply_delegated_batch’s _terminal_attempt sets lease.state=released before apply returns; resolve_parked already maps policy_pause→escalate_resume, projects blocked pending_gates with requested_at+T deadlines, and reuses proceed/blocked subject keys; ExecutionAdapter.resume already enforces gate-decision approval_ref for policy_pause. The plan composes these seams rather than inventing a second gate path.
